title: Quant profile publish gateway and performance sentinel for mixed-precision variants
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a publish-and-verify gateway for quantization profiles (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) that enforces artifact signing, executes a telemetry-driven canary, and pins a stable profile to model versions. This ticket covers the API surface for publishing profiles, the canary execution harness, the performance sentinel that detects regressions versus the pinned baseline, and rollback/fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Profile publish API accepts signed profile artifacts and returns a profile_id and computed checksums
Automated canary runs against a representative prompt set within customer-configured resource bounds
Performance sentinel computes quality and latency deltas against pinned baseline and raises alerts when thresholds are breached
Profiles can be pinned to model-version identifiers and exposed via model metadata API
Rollback path exists: on failed canary or regression exceedance, profile is not promoted and traffic routes to fallback variant automatically
End-to-end test in CI that simulates publish -> canary -> promote -> pin -> rollback paths runs deterministically
decisions: Use artifact signing (Ed25519) and store signature with profile metadata to prevent tampering
Canary will run on a dedicated small GPU pool to preserve production capacity and ensure consistent env
Regression thresholds: quality delta > 2% relative decrease OR latency p95 increase > 10% triggers block
We will use paired statistical test (Wilcoxon signed-rank) on the canonical prompt set for quality comparisons; require p < 0.05 and effect size threshold to consider significant
Profiles stored in profile-index service with immutable versioned keys; pinning creates a mapping model_version -> profile_id
Promote-on-pass: promotion requires passing canary and passing CI smoke harness; promotion will create a changelog entry and optional rollout schedule

implementation_notes: API: POST /v1/models/{model_version}/quant-profiles -> accepts tar.gz artifact + manifest.json + signature; returns profile_id
Artifact manifest fields: model_hash, quant_method, precision_bits, codegen_flags, tested_sequence_lengths, sample_prompt_sha256_list, baseline_metrics (lat, qscore)
Profile-index changes: add columns 'profile_state' (draft, canary, promoted, pinned, revoked), 'canary_runs' (list of run ids as CSV), 'promoted_at' timestamp
Canary harness: orchestrate N runs across representative prompt set; collect metrics: generation_quality (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity/custom_eval), p50/p95 latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, mem_peak_mb
Promotion guard: require canary success and CI smoke green; promote action triggers pin if user requested 'pin_on_promote' flag
Fallback policy: on in-flight regression detection, route traffic to next compatible promoted profile or to float (unquantized) variant depending on SLO and cost policy
risks: False positives in quality regression detection for small canary sample sets; mitigate by requiring both statistical significance and minimum absolute effect size
Canary runs consuming GPU credit and affecting capacity if not isolated properly
Pinned profiles might mask model drifting; need periodic re-evaluations and drift alerts
Complexity of supporting multiple quant methods with differing compatibility guarantees (e.g., AWQ memory layout differences)
qa_plan: Add unit tests for signature verification and manifest parsing
CI e2e test that uploads a synthetic profile artifact and asserts canary lifecycle (draft -> canary -> promoted -> pinned)
Manual QA: run canary with long-seq prompts and inspect latency tail behavior and KV cache correctness
Load test: simulate 100 concurrent publishes to ensure profile-index transactional behavior
